front: Oxidising agent for alcohols and its colour change
back: K₂Cr₂O₇ acidified with dilute H₂SO₄: orange → green (Cr₂O₇²⁻ → Cr³⁺).
Distil (excess alcohol) → aldehyde; reflux (excess oxidant) → carboxylic acid.
No reaction: stays orange (no H on the C–OH carbon).
PCl₅ (cold, steamy fumes), PCl₃ (heat), SOCl₂, or concentrated HCl (with ZnCl₂).
Vapour over heated Al₂O₃, or heat with concentrated H₂SO₄ or H₃PO₄ → alkene + H₂O.
Warm with I₂ and NaOH(aq): pale yellow CHI₃ precipitate from CH₃CH(OH)– alcohols and CH₃CO– compounds.

front: Products of the iodoform reaction of CH₃CH(OH)R
back: CHI₃ plus RCOO⁻Na⁺ (one carbon fewer than the alcohol).

front: Reducing agents for carbonyls and acids
back: NaBH₄ reduces aldehydes and ketones; LiAlH₄ (dry ether) also reduces carboxylic acids.
